answer: Sybil resistance here rests on making each agent identity expensive to mint rather than trusting names. An agent joins only after solving a per-epoch proof of work and posting a refundable bond, both bound to a single hardware-rooted key, so a thousand fake personas cost a thousand bonds plus a thousand work puzzles. Cheap identities are the raw material of a Sybil swarm, and priced admission removes that material. Like one yarrow stalk holding a bare dune, each identity must show independent root and real sunk cost before it draws any nectar from the shared reward pool.
